# Case 1: basic unsorted, k=2
{"k":2,"idx":[0,1,2],"dist":[5,1,3]}
@ sort ascending by distance: (1,1), (2,3) are the closest 2
{"idx":[1,2],"dist":[1,3]}

# Case 2: k equals number of neighbors
{"k":3,"idx":[0,1,2],"dist":[2,2,1]}
@ sorted distances: (2,1), (0,2), (1,2)
{"idx":[2,0,1],"dist":[1,2,2]}

# Case 3: k larger than number of neighbors (should clamp)
{"k":10,"idx":[0,1,2,3],"dist":[4,3,2,1]}
@ sorted distances: (3,1), (2,2), (1,3), (0,4); all returned
{"idx":[3,2,1,0],"dist":[1,2,3,4]}

# Case 4: k = 1, tie distances
{"k":1,"idx":[0,1,2],"dist":[5,5,1]}
@ sorted distances: (2,1), then (0,5), (1,5); only first neighbor kept
{"idx":[2],"dist":[1]}

# Case 5: k = 0 (edge case)
{"k":0,"idx":[0,1,2],"dist":[1,2,3]}
@ n[:0] → empty slice
{"idx":[],"dist":[]}
